title: How Harry Burns of New Orleans began booking the band
summary: In McAlester, Oklahoma, agent Harry Burns, born Bernstein, meets Fields and books three or four dates.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: And then another--as I said perhaps so many in between, almost too numerous to name, but one I will not pass up, was Harry Burns. It was kind of odd and strange the way it came about. I was in McAlester, Oklahoma, which you consider that my territory booking, and Harry Burns then was booking--do you remember the Wings Over Joy (phonetic spelling), the gospel group, well he was booking them and he just knew the country from A to Z, where you'd be good when it's good in this town and this and that, and he wanted to know if I travelled, did I go out of the area. I told him yes; so he said I'd certainly like to book you, and I gave him one of my cards and he said you will hear from me. Sure enough, he did contact me and booked three or four dates.
Did I ever say anything to you about the incident about the guy who said you
can't stop the dancing; do you have that on tape or were we just talking?
No, you didn't tell me that, but first, you did tell me Herb Burns' name was something else.
I understand it was Bernstein, but he didn't want--you know, he didn't want--a lot of times people don't want being known that you are a Jew. So I understand he changed it to Burns.
Harry Burns, National Orchestra Service of New Orleans; and he booked a date or two for me after I few months I heard from him.
